chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they accept from his whispers/doubts.
And He did not grant him authority over the believers.

key_terms.أَوْهَامِهِمْ: Whispers, doubts, or presumptions (plural of wahm)

ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's *hakimiyyah* (authority) over believers is not inherent but contingent upon their voluntary acceptance of his whispers, thereby emphasizing human agency in spiritual struggle. This distinction refutes the idea of absolute demonic control, aligning with the Shia doctrine that while Satan tempts, he cannot compel the faithful unless they consent. The narration underscores that spiritual elevation depends on actively rejecting these whispers, a concept central to the Shia understanding of *fitrah* and free will.
